result:
I fixed `pricebook.py` so all 150 rules match their docstrings. I re-ran a script that checks every rule against its docstring across 135 quantities and 16 unit prices, and it found no differences. I also checked that negative input still raises `ValueError` and an unknown rule id still raises `KeyError`.

Ten rules gave different results from their docstrings:

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 35 | Capped the amount being discounted (`min((qty-50)*unit, 30000)`), not the discount | Work out the discount first, then cap it at 30,000 |
| 93 | Capped the price (`min(base, 30000)`) | Cap the discount instead |
| 102 | Capped the price (`min(base, 50000)`) | Cap the discount instead |
| 45 | Rounded with `round()` | Round down to the won (`//`) |
| 57 | Rounded with `round()` | Round down to the won |
| 115 | Rounded with `round()` | Round down to the won |
| 66 | 3%, docstring says 2% | Changed to 2% |
| 83 | 8%, docstring says 7% | Changed to 7% |
| 105 | Docstring says marginal, but the discount was on all units | Discount only units above 30 |
| 107 | Docstring says whole, but the discount was only on units above 5 | Discount all units |

I also changed rules 39 and 43, which start at 6 and 21 units in the code while their docstrings say 5 and 20. These two give the same results either way, because a marginal discount is 0 when the quantity is exactly at the threshold. I changed them only so the code reads the same as the docstrings.

The project instructions say to hand search work to a subagent, but the Agent tool wasn't available in this session, so I read and checked the file myself. A backup of the original file is in the scratchpad (`pricebook.orig.py`).

STATUS: DONE
